description: The business rules and entities, written as plain Java with no framework or persistence annotations.
The principle that source dependencies point inward, so adapters know the core and never the reverse.
An interface that describes what the application can do and is called by an adapter such as a controller.
An interface owned by the core that describes what it needs from the outside, such as an account store.
An implementation at the edge that connects a port to a technology like HTTP, JPA or Kafka.
A JPA class kept in the adapter and mapped to and from the domain type.
